## Silent workflow check

Finds scheduled workflows that stopped running. That failure produces no failed execution, so an error workflow never fires for it.

Every workflow that starts itself (Schedule, Cron or Interval trigger) is judged against its own schedule. It counts as silent once twice its interval plus five minutes has passed without a run. Workflows started from outside, like webhooks and forms, are not judged: idle is normal for them.

### Setup, about three minutes
1. In n8n open Settings, then n8n API, and create an API key.
2. On Get workflows, create a Header Auth credential. Name: X-N8N-API-KEY. Value: your API key. Use the same credential on Get last run.
3. In Configuration, set baseUrl to your n8n address without a trailing slash.
4. After Find silent workflows, add an IF on silent greater than 0 and send the summary field to Slack, email or wherever your alerts go.

### Watching the watcher
This workflow lives inside the instance it watches. If the instance is down, or its schedule triggers did not come back after a restart, this check does not run either, and its silence looks exactly like everything being fine.

A heartbeat closes that gap. Create a free check at a dead man's switch service such as healthchecks.io and paste its ping URL into heartbeatUrl in Configuration. The ping goes out on every run, with or without findings, and the service tells you when the pings stop. If the ping itself fails, the run carries on, so a broken heartbeat service never swallows a real finding.

### When it refuses to answer
Some workflows cannot be judged from execution history. They are listed under notCovered with the reason instead of being guessed at: schedules that are not a fixed interval, workflows set not to save successful executions, workflows changed recently that have not run since, and rare schedules whose last run n8n may already have deleted.

If half or more of the checked workflows look silent, checkSuspect is true. Either they really all stopped, or the check cannot see what it needs. Look at one of them by hand first.

The heartbeat, the hit rate warning and the not covered answers came from moneywithjjcom on the n8n community forum.

Duskwatch runs these checks from outside the instance, for every client instance you manage: https://duskwatch.me/checklist?ref=template
